sources.entry: Dokploy | Deployment platform for apps and databases, a Heroku alternative

summary.one_liner: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS) for deploying and managing applications and databases on your own VPS.
summary.what_it_does: Dokploy deploys applications of many types (the README names Node.js, PHP, Python, Go, Ruby) and creates and manages databases including MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MariaDB, libsql, and Redis. It can automate database backups to an external storage destination and natively supports Docker Compose. It integrates with Traefik for routing and load balancing and offers one-click deployment of open-source templates such as Plausible, Pocketbase, and Calcom. It monitors CPU, memory, storage, and network usage per resource and can ship logs and metrics to services such as Grafana, Datadog, and AWS CloudWatch. It also supports multi-node scaling via Docker Swarm, deployment to remote servers, notifications via Slack, Discord, Telegram, and Email, and management through a CLI and API.
use_cases: self-host a Heroku alternative on a VPS
deploy web apps and APIs without manual Docker setup
run and back up PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, or Redis databases
one-click install open-source apps like Plausible or Pocketbase
manage Docker Compose stacks through a web panel
monitor container resource usage and ship logs to Grafana or Datadog
deploy apps to multiple remote servers
how_to_run: Run the install script on a VPS: curl -sSL <url> | bash (the URL is missing from the README text as extracted)
Read the detailed documentation at docs.dokploy.com
notable: Full PaaS in one self-hosted package covering apps, databases, backups, and monitoring
Built-in Traefik routing with automatic integration
Ships container logs and metrics to many observability backends, tagged by project, environment, and application
Offers a hosted Dokploy Cloud option as an alternative to self-hosting
